pending.thesis: Strategy v1 (November 11, 2026). Initiate a modest $150 (15% of $1,000 equity) long-only SPY paper allocation, with a 4–8 week broad-market exposure horizon and daily review, while retaining approximately $850 cash before modeled costs. This is an exposure decision, NOT a proven near-term forecast. As of the November 12 premarket review, GitHub state records $1,000 cash, zero positions, zero pending orders, and four accepted prior stock HOLD decisions (Nov 6, 9, 10, 11); no duplicate open BUY exists. The collector succeeded at 2026-11-12T09:51:40Z with no errors, but the latest COMPLETED stock bars are November 11, not November 12 live executable quotes: SPY $759.81, RSP $222.65, IWM $283.09, QQQ $690.38, XLV $188.95, XLE $63.37, SGOV $100.52, NVDA $173.73. The $1,000 passive SPY benchmark began at the November 4 $766.81 close and is marked $990.87 at the November 11 close; the all-cash account remains $1,000, ahead by $9.13 purely because it was uninvested, not because a directional signal was demonstrated. The S&P 500 rose 1.31% and Nasdaq 1.60% on November 11 amid strong CoreWeave-linked AI infrastructure optimism; the November 12 Reuters premarket report instead shows S&P 500 futures down approximately 0.31%, Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.64%, and NVDA down around 6% amid leadership uncertainty. These are time-specific futures/indications, not synchronized executable SPY quotes. November 10 hotter inflation and expected December Fed tightening, Friday November 13 PPI, and AI leadership/valuation shocks argue against deploying the full account. However, v1 strategy explicitly weighs modest diversified SPY exposure against indefinite cash, and diversified participation over weeks has a coherent risk-premium rationale without requiring a claimed short-term forecasting edge. SPY is a large established broad-market ETF already supported and tracked; its liquidity is preferable to speculative single names, although live spreads and today's actual fill price are unverified. RSP would reduce megacap concentration but change factor exposure; IWM adds smaller-company rate sensitivity; QQQ concentrates the very AI/technology leadership risk now prominent; XLE and XLV are sector tilts without stronger independently established theses; SGOV is a short-duration rate reference whose distribution accounting is not yet modeled. pending.risk_notes: The allocation risks loss from hotter November 13 PPI, Fed tightening, valuation compression, AI/semiconductor leadership instability, geopolitical/oil shocks and a gap between the observed November 11 SPY close and the future eligible simulated open. SPY is diversified but still cap-weighted and exposed to megacap technology. Cash could outperform if declines resume; conversely leaving 85% in cash creates opportunity cost if equities rally. Estimated model fee 0.10% plus adverse slippage 0.05% is about $0.225 for a $150 one-way notional; eventual exit incurs costs too, and real spreads/market impact are not represented. $150 is above the $10 minimum and well below the $350 35%-of-equity per-asset cap, with no other positions or pending orders. No real money, broker, leverage, shorts, derivatives, crypto-account activity or backdating. No claim of skill or executed fill.
